summary: Iteration 6 testing of Neural — PayPal sandbox subscriptions, Resend receipts, dynamic admin pricing, admin user-delete + clear-alerts, share rate limit, plan-upgrade gating. Backend: 22/22 tests pass (100%). Frontend: Pricing page renders correctly with PayPal SDK (4 iframes loaded for Pro+Elite buttons), sandbox banner visible, all 3 plan cards present. Admin page shows new pricing editor module + per-user action icons (Reset, BellOff/clear-alerts, Trash/delete) on every user row. Non-admin user (demo@stockai.io) is correctly redirected from /admin to /dashboard.

minor.issue: Endpoint returns 'No active subscription' for users without paypal_subscription_id, but the user.plan is left untouched. If a user's DB record has plan=pro/elite (admin-elevated) but no PayPal sub, calling /cancel returns 400 and never resets them to free. Acceptable for MVP but worth a UX note: the Cancel button is hidden for these users so it's only reachable via API.

When PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID env is unset (current state), webhooks are accepted, logged to db.webhook_events with verified=false, and never mutate user/subscription state. This is by design but means recurring renewal receipts and subscription lifecycle updates from PayPal will silently no-op until WEBHOOK_ID is configured. Action: register a webhook in PayPal dashboard and set PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID before going live.

integration_issues.flow: Pricing page — Cancel subscription button visibility
integration_issues.issue: tiers@demo.io is documented as 'pro' plan in test_credentials.md, but the nav badge currently reads 'FREE PLAN' — user.plan in DB has likely been overwritten by an earlier admin/cancel flow. Because the Cancel/Downgrade buttons only render when user.plan != 'free' AND paypal_subscription_id is present, the buttons never appear for this user. Cosmetic for QA but worth a re-seed of tiers@demo.io to plan='pro' if this test fixture is meant to demo the cancel flow. Actual cancel logic (POST /api/billing/cancel returning 400 for no-sub users) tested green via API.

issues: The two pricing inputs render empty for ~500ms before useEffect populates them with current DB values. Add an initial loading skeleton or set inputs to placeholders to avoid the visual flicker.

critical_code_review_comments: billing.py: /billing/config calls get_plan_ids() which lazy-creates PayPal product+plans on first hit. First request can take 5-15s. Consider warming this on startup or showing a loader on the Pricing page; currently the PayPal buttons render without a clear pending state during the cold call.

billing.py: /billing/activate awaits send_receipt_email() inline — if Resend is down or rate-limits, the activate call will block on it. The comment says 'fire-and-forget' but it is awaited. Wrap it with asyncio.create_task or try/except so a Resend failure doesn't 500 a successful subscription activation.

paypal.py: get_plan_ids() rotates plans on every price change but does NOT update existing PayPal subscribers — by design, but worth surfacing in admin UI: 'X existing subscribers stay at old price until they re-subscribe.' (Already in success message, good.)

admin.py: delete_user cascades correctly to watchlist/analyses/alerts/shared_verdicts/quick_jobs/disclaimers/subscriptions but does NOT call PayPal to cancel any active subscription — orphan PayPal subs will keep billing. Consider calling cancel_subscription(sid) before deleting if user.paypal_subscription_id exists.

analysis.py: share rate-limit check uses iso(now_utc() - timedelta(days=1)) — a sliding 24h window, not a calendar day. Spec says 'daily share-link rate limit'; sliding-window is fine but document it. Current implementation: created_at comparisons use ISO string lex order which is correct for UTC ISO timestamps.

config.py: PLANS share_per_day values are 5/50/None as spec'd. plans_with_live_pricing() only patches price_usd, share_per_day stays from PLANS — meaning admin cannot change the share limit at runtime, only the price. If admins should also tune share_per_day, add it to db.settings/pricing. (Out of scope for this iteration, just flagging.)

pricing.py: get_pricing reads from db.settings on every call — adds a mongo round-trip to every /plans, /billing/config, and /admin/pricing hit. Consider in-process caching with a small TTL (e.g., 30s) or a settings-change pubsub.
paypal.py: _token_cache is module-level dict — fine for single-worker uvicorn but breaks under multi-worker deploys. If you ever scale to >1 worker, move to redis or per-request fetch.
